target_customer: Restaurants, hotels, CPG brands and retailers in Mexico buying fresh produce, later small and mid-size food distributors
problem: Fresh produce buyers in Latin America plan, order and track purchases through fragmented, manual channels. Alima digitized procurement with ordering, expense management and logistics.
business_model: B2B procurement marketplace and ordering software, margin on goods sold and later software for distributors
product_category: Fresh food procurement and supply chain software

founders.name: Jorge Vizcayno
founders.background_notes: YC page: Head of Tech at ByPrice; TechCrunch calls him mechatronics engineer with ML and data science background and former CTO of Byprice.

founders.name: Blanca Espinosa
education: MBA, Escuela Europea de Direccion y Empresa
founders.background_notes: YC page: 15+ years in growth, marketing and business development.

founders.name: Jorge Moreno Sanchez Briseno
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as a former Alima co-founder and COO.

competitors.name: Frubana
competitors.what: Colombia based B2B platform buying produce from farmers and delivering to restaurants and small retailers, operating in Colombia, Mexico and Brazil; the CEO called it the closest competitor
competitors.traction_then: Active customers grew sixfold and sales tripled in the prior year
competitors.funding_then: 65M Series B led by GGV Capital in 2021

technical_complexity.rationale: Ordering software and supplier catalogues are standard web engineering; the difficulty was operations and logistics in Mexico.

defensibility.rationale: Supplier relationships and order data helped, but a better funded rival already ran the same wedge and software was copyable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Frubana was the named closest rival; CB Insights lists it as dead per a search summary. Alima was bought by Pepper in March 2026 and the founders joined Pepper's leadership.

market_need_then: TechCrunch reported revenue up 10x since January 2022, about 600 customers and 800 SKUs by September 2022, showing demand for digital produce ordering among restaurants and hotels.

branding.domain_note: Uses alima.la (country code style .la domain) per the YC page.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain operational language aimed at food service buyers

brand_strength.rationale: TechCrunch and LatamList covered the seed round, but no brand story, community or merch was found; the name is shared with unrelated companies.

pivots.from: Fresh produce procurement marketplace for buyers in Mexico
pivots.to: Ordering platform for small and mid-size food distributors
pivots.why: TNW describes the product as an ordering platform for distributors starting with produce procurement; the reason for the change is not stated

outcome_analysis: Alima grew quickly after Winter 2022 YC, reporting 10x revenue growth and about 600 customers by September 2022 on a 1.5 million dollar seed. In March 2026 Pepper acquired it, with terms undisclosed and the two founders joining Pepper's leadership, so the outcome looks like a small team exit into a distributor technology platform rather than a standalone scale up; no shutdown cause applies.
notes: TechCrunch and TNW both state the 1.5M seed; CB Insights total of 2M differs and is not recorded as a round. The Logistics World article says 1.5 million pesos, likely an error. Former name Neutro comes from a search summary of PitchBook or CB Insights, date unknown. Pivot date is approximate and the exact change is only described by TNW. Alima's own site fetch returned only a title (platform for food service providers). Total raised and any later rounds are unknown, so coverage is partial. Success factor is a judgment from reported growth.
